1294.1: Raag Kanra, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. Meeting the holy ones, my mind has turned green (with life). To the holy ones I offer myself, a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice; joining (their) company, I have crossed over (the world-ocean). O Lord, Har Har, O God, show your mercy; I have fallen at the feet of the holy ones. Blessed, blessed are the holy ones who have known the Lord God; meeting the Saadh (the holy one), even the fallen one is saved. The mind wanders and wanders in many, many ways; meeting the Saadh, (it) has been brought under control, as the fisherman cast his net in the water, caught the fish and carried it off, held fast. Good and noble are the Sants (saints) of the Lord, the Sants; meeting the Sants, the filth (of the mind) has been washed off. All the sin of Haumai (ego) has gone out, as a cloth is made (clean) with soap. The Master wrote (it) on (my) forehead, on my brow, from the very beginning; (so I) have set the feet of the Guru, the True Guru, in (my) heart. (I) have found God, who shatters all poverty and pain; through the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) servant Nanak has been delivered. ॥4॥
Chaupade (chau, four; pad, stanza): hymns of four stanzas.
1294.2: Raag Kanra, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). My mind has become the dust of the Sants' feet; joining (their) company I heard the telling of the Lord, Har Har, and (my) raw, undyed mind was steeped in the colour of the Lord. We are heedless and unaware and do not know (his) state and extent; the Guru has made (us) mindful and alert. God, merciful to the lowly, has taken (us) as his own, and in (our) minds (we) repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har. If the Sants of the Lord, beloved of my mind, should meet (me), I would cut out my heart and give it to them. The Lord's Sants met (me), and the Lord was met; (they) have made us, the fallen, pure. The Lord's servants are called exalted in the world, on meeting whom even stones are soaked through. I cannot describe the glory of (the Lord's) servants; the Lord, Har Har, has made them exalted. O Lord, God, my Master, you are the great banker, and we are traders; give (us) the capital (of the Name). O God, show kindness to servant Nanak, that (he) may load (his pack) with the goods of the Lord, Har Har. ॥4॥
1295.1: Raag Kanra, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O mind, repeat the Name of Ram (the Lord): (it brings) light. Meeting the Lord's Sants, love (for him) has taken hold; (the mind is) detached in the very midst of the household. In (our) hearts we have repeated the Name of the Lord, Narhari; God, the merciful, has shown mercy. Night and day there is bliss, the mind has blossomed; in the hope of meeting (him), efforts have sprung up. We have set our love on the Lord, the Master, with every breath and every morsel we have taken; (so) in an instant (our) sins were burnt up, and the nooses of Maya were broken. What are we, mere worms, and what deeds can we do? We fools and simpletons, that God has saved. Full of faults, heavy as stones, we joined the Sat Sangat (the company of the true) and have crossed over, carried across (by him). Of all the creation the Lord of the world has made, all are high; we are low, (sunk) in vice. In the Guru's company (God) has wiped away our faults, and has united servant Nanak with God, at his side. ॥4॥
Narhari (nar, man; hari, lion): Narasimha, the Man-Lion in whose form, in the Puranas, God saved Prahlad; in Gurbani, a name of God.
1295.2: Raag Kanra, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Through the Guru's word my mind has repeated the Name of Ram. The Lord of the world, Har Har, has shown mercy; evil-mindedness, the love of another and all craving have gone. Many are the forms and colours of the Lord; Ram pervades every heart, hidden. The Lord's Sants met (me), and the Lord was revealed; the shutters of Maya have opened. Great, very great is the glory of the Sants who, as lovers, have enshrined in their hearts the Lord, the source of delight. The Lord's Sants met (me), and the Lord was met, as the calf (rejoices) on seeing the cow. The Lord, Har Har, (dwells) in the Lord's Sants; those servants are exalted among all people. In their hearts the fragrance of the Lord has come to dwell, and the stench (of vice) has gone. O God, your servants you yourself have made; O Lord, keep (them) safe, making (them) your own. The Lord is servant Nanak's friend and brother; mother, father, kin and relation, the Lord is (all). ॥4॥
1295.3: Raag Kanra, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O my mind, repeat within (your) consciousness the Name of Ram, the Lord, Har Har. The treasure of the Lord, Har Har, is enclosed in the fortress of Maya; through the Guru's Shabad the fortress has been won. (The soul) has wandered and wandered much in false delusion, lured by attachment and love for son and wife. Like the fleeting shade of a tree, the wall of the body perishes in an instant. The exalted servants (of God) are as dear to us as life; meeting them, faith arises in the mind; (the mind) is won over by Ram, pervading within the heart, and with love and affection dwells on Ram, the Eternal. Good are the Sants of the Lord, the Sants, meeting whom the mind is dyed in the colour (of his love). The Lord's colour never fades, never comes off; by love for the Lord one reaches and meets the Lord, Har Har. We wrongdoers committed many sins; the Guru has cut them away, cut them clean away. (The Guru) has put the medicine of the Name of the Lord, Har Har, in (our) mouths; O servant Nanak, (so) the fallen have become pure. ॥4॥
1296.1: Raag Kanra, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O mind, repeat the Name of Ram, the Lord of the world. O True Guru, giving (your) hand, (you) have drawn out those fallen into the whirlpool of poisonous Maya. O fearless, stainless Master, O Narhari, save us, sinners (heavy as) stones. (We are) lured by lust, anger and greed for Maya; (yet) in the company of wood, iron has floated across. You are the great Being, greatly inaccessible, beyond the reach of the senses; we have searched and searched, and have not found (your) depth. You are beyond, beyond, beyond the farthest beyond, O Master; you yourself know yourself, O Lord of the world. Joining the Sat Sangat, on the path of the Saadh, (I) have meditated on the Name of the unseen One beyond the senses. Joining the Sangat, (I) have heard the telling of the Lord, Har Har, and repeated (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, the One whose telling is beyond telling. O our God, Lord of the world, Master of the earth, Lord of all creation, save us. Servant Nanak is the servant of the servants of (your) servants; O God, have mercy, keep (him) with (your) devotees. ॥4॥
1296.2: Raag Kanra, Ghar 5, Partal, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O mind, repeat (the Name of) Ram, Gopal (the sustainer of the world). (The Name of) the Lord is a jewel, a gem, a ruby; through the Guru, fashion (it) in the mint. O mind, the Lord is merciful. Your virtues are inaccessible, beyond the reach of the senses; what can one poor tongue tell (of them), O Ram, Ram, Ram, Ram, O beloved? Your telling, dear Lord, is beyond telling; you, you, you alone know (it); repeating (the Name of) the Lord I am delighted, delighted, delighted. The Lord is the companion of our life, our Master; the Lord is (our) friend; in my mind, in my body and on my tongue, the Lord, Har Hare Hare, the Name of Ram, is wealth and riches. O friend, the one whose fortune it is has gained her Husband (the Lord); through the Guru's teaching she sings the praises of the Lord, Har Har Hare Hare; I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice (to her); I, servant Nanak, repeating (the Name of) the Lord, am delighted, delighted, delighted. ॥2॥
Partal: a setting in which the rhythm (taal) changes again and again as the hymn is sung.
Ho ho: a call of address (O!) sung in the Rahao lines of these shabads; the meaning gives it as the one the shabad addresses.
1296.3: Raag Kanra, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Sing the praises of the Lord, the Master of the world; one should make the one tongue into twenty lakh (tongues); through the Shabad, repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, who alone is worthy to be repeated. O brother, the Lord is the master of mercy. O Lord, my Master, show mercy and set us to the Lord's service; O Lord of the world, repeating and repeating the Lord, repeating and repeating the Lord, may (I) keep chanting (your) chant. Your servants who repeat (the Name of) Ram are exalted; to them I offer myself, a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice. O Lord, you are great, the greatest of the great, high and exalted; you do whatever pleases you. Servant Nanak has drunk the Amrit (the nectar that gives spiritual life) through the Guru's teaching; blessed, blessed, blessed, blessed, blessed is the Guru, worthy of all praise. ॥2॥
1297.1: Raag Kanra, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Dwell in (your) mind on Ram, on Ram, who has no form and no outline, and is the greatest. Join the Sat Sangat and dwell on Ram; O brother, great is the fortune on (such a one's) forehead. In whatever house or mansion the Lord's praise is sung, in that home there is bliss upon bliss; dwell on Ram, Ram, Ram. Sing the praises of the Name of Ram, of the beloved Lord; through the teaching of the Guru, the Guru, the True Guru, peace comes; dwell on the Lord, Har Hare Har Hare Hare, on Ram, Ram, Ram. O Lord, you are the support of all creation, the merciful, the Creator; all is you, you, you, O Ram, Ram, Ram. Servant Nanak has come to (your) refuge; give (him) the Guru's teaching; dwell on Ram, Ram, Ram. ॥2॥
1297.2: Raag Kanra, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). I kiss, I kiss the feet of the True Guru, meeting whom the road to the Lord (becomes) smooth. Dwell on the Lord, the sweet essence; drink down the essence of the Lord in deep draughts; O brother, (this gift) the Lord writes on the forehead. (Some) perform the rites of the six duties and make a great, great display; the Siddhas (yogis of perfect powers), the seekers and the yogis grow matted hair upon matted hair; (but) by putting on (religious) garb union with the Lord God is not found; the Lord is found in the Sat Sangat, through the teaching of the Guru, the Guru, as the Sants throw open (the mind's) shutters. You are beyond the farthest beyond, O Master, utterly unfathomable; you fill the water and the land; the Lord is One, the One alone, and all creation is the One Lord's. You know all ways, you yourself understand; O God of servant Nanak, O Lord, you dwell in every heart, in every heart, in every heart. ॥2॥
The six duties (khat karam) are a Brahmin's: to study and to teach, to perform sacrifice and to have it performed, to give alms and to receive them.
1297.3: Raag Kanra, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O mind, repeat (the Name of) Gobind (the Lord of the universe), Madho, the Lord, Har Har, inaccessible and unfathomable; through the understanding of the Guru's teaching the Lord God is found; O mind, (by those on whose) forehead (this) is written from the very beginning. Gathering the poison of Maya, (one) thinks up many vices; peace is found (this way): dwell on the Lord in the company of the Sants, the Sants, meeting the True Guru, the Guru, the Saadh. As slag of burnt iron (manoor), touched by the paaras (the touchstone that turns iron to gold), becomes gold, so the fallen, joining the Sangat, become pure through the Guru's teaching, pure indeed. As much iron floats across with wood, so sinners cross over in the company of the holy, the holy, in the company of the Guru, the True Guru, the Guru, the Saadh. There are four castes and four stages of life; whoever (among them) meets the Guru, the Guru, O Nanak, crosses over himself and carries all his family across. ॥2॥
Madho (maa, Maya or Lakshmi, and dhav, husband): a name of God.
1297.4: Raag Kanra, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Sing the praise of the Lord God; in singing (his) praise, sins depart; through the understanding of the Guru's teaching, hear his praises with (your) ears; O brother, the Lord is merciful. Your servants meditate on (you) with one mind, one heart; those holy ones find peace, repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har, the treasure. O God, O Lord God, meeting the Saadh, the holy ones, the Guru, the True Guru, they sing your praises. O Master, those in whose hearts you (dwell) gain the fruit of peace; they have crossed the world-ocean; know them to be the Lord's devotees. Set us to their service, O Lord, set us (to it), O Lord; O Lord of servant Nanak, you, you, you, you, you are the Lord God. ॥2॥
1298.1: Raag Kanra, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. One should sing the praises of Gopal, the treasure of mercy. O True Guru, destroyer of sorrow and giver of peace, meeting whom all fulfilment comes. As one remembers the Naam, it gives support to the mind, and carries millions of wrongdoers across in an instant. The one to whose mind his own Guru comes has no sorrow, not a jot, even in a dream. The one whom his own True Guru protects, that person tastes with his tongue the essence of the Lord. Says Nanak, (the one on whom) the Guru has shown kindness, his face has become bright, here and hereafter. ॥4॥
1298.2: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). You alone I worship, O my own Master; standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, with every breath, every breath, every breath I repeat (the Name of) the Lord. The Naam has come to dwell in the heart of that one to whom the Master has given (this) gift. Peace has come into the heart of that one who has met the Master through the Guru's word. That one alone is skilled in every art to whom the Guru has given the mantra of the Naam. Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to that one who in Kalyug has found the Name. ॥4॥
1298.3: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Sing the praises of God, O my tongue. Bow to the Sants again and again; there (in them) dwell the feet of the revered Gobind. By many kinds of effort I cannot find (God's) door; when (he) becomes merciful, then I meditate on the Lord, Har Har. Doing millions of rites, the body is not purified; in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) the mind is awakened. Thirst was not quenched by Maya of many colours; taking the Naam, every comfort has been found. When the Supreme Lord became merciful, says Nanak, then the entanglements fell away. ॥4॥
1298.4: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ask of Gobind for such (a gift): the service of the Sants, the company of the Saadh, and the Name of the Lord, repeating which (one reaches) the supreme state; the worship of (his) feet, the refuge of the Master, and (to take) as well-being whatever dear God does. This body, so hard to obtain, bears fruit (for the one) on whom the True Guru shows kindness. Ignorance, doubt and the dwelling-place of sorrows are destroyed (for the one) in whose heart the Guru's feet dwell. The one who has meditated on God with love in the Saadh Sangat, says Nanak, has found the Perfect One. ॥4॥
1299.1: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Devotion befits the devotees alone; their bodies and minds are absorbed in the Master; (he) has united (them) with himself. The singer (the world) sings her songs, (but) those are saved in whose hearts (God) dwells. The one who serves the dishes has (only) seen them; those who have eaten the meal are satisfied. The actor dresses up in many disguises, (yet) as he was, so he is seen. All talking and getting others to talk is entanglement; O servant Nanak, (living) the Truth is the excellent deed. ॥4॥
1299.2: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O God,) your servant, hearing the Lord's praise, is uplifted with joy. Seeing God's glory, the mind is lit up; wherever I look, (he) is there. (He) is beyond all, higher than the beyond, deep, profound and unfathomable. Like warp and weft (he) is joined with his devotees; from his servant (he) has drawn aside the veil. By the Guru's grace Nanak sings (his) praises, absorbed in the samadhi of Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise). ॥4॥
1299.3: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (I) have come to the Sants for my own deliverance. Beholding (them), one becomes pure; (they) have made firm (within) the mantra of the Lord, Har Har. Diseases are cut away and minds made pure, (once) the medicine of the Lord, Har Har, is taken. (They) have become steady and dwell in the abode of peace, and do not run anywhere again. By the Sants' grace (their) families and people are carried across; O Nanak, (they) are not stained by Maya. ॥4॥
1299.4: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). All envy of others has been forgotten since I found the Saadh Sangat. There is no enemy and no stranger; with everyone I am at one. Whatever God has done, (I) have accepted as good; this wisdom (I) have received from the Saadh. The One God pervades all; seeing (him) again and again, Nanak blossoms (with joy). ॥3॥
1299.5: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Dear Master, (I lean on) your support. My honour and standing rest on you; (I have) your shelter, your refuge. In you is (my) hope, in you (my) trust; your Name is what (I) take and hold in (my) heart. Yours is (my) strength, with you (I am) at ease; whatever you say, that alone is to be done. By your kindness and mercy I find peace; be merciful, and the terrifying world-ocean will be crossed. The Name of the Lord, the gift of fearlessness, has been received; Nanak has laid his head at the feet of the Sants. ॥2॥
1300.1: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In the refuge of the Saadh I have fixed (my) mind on (God's) feet; (the world) I had heard spoken of as a dream I have now seen to be a dream, since the True Guru made firm (in me) the mantra of the Naam. (The mind) was not satisfied by power, youth and wealth, and ran (after them) again and again; (now) peace has been found, all thirst is quenched and calm has come, singing (God's) praises. Without understanding, (one) is like a beast, caught in doubt and in attachment to Maya. In the Saadh Sangat the noose of Jam (the messenger of Death) has been cut; Nanak has merged in Sahaj. ॥2॥
1300.2: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). With the Lord's feet in (your) heart, sing (his praises); remember again and again, and meditate every day on (him), cooling, the very form of peace and calm. All hopes are fulfilled, and the pain of millions of births departs. Acts of merit, charity and many rites (lie in this): be absorbed in the company of the Saadh. Fevers and torments are ended, O Nanak, and death does not devour (one) again. ॥2॥
1300.3: Raag Kanra, Ghar 3, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. One should speak of the knowledge of God in the company of the Sants. Remembering the Supreme God, the perfect, supreme Light, honour is received. Comings and goings have ended and weariness has gone, remembering (him) in the company of the Saadh; in the love of the Supreme Lord the fallen are made pure within a moment. Whoever speaks and hears the Kirtan (songs of God's praise) of the Lord, his evil-mindedness is destroyed; he attains all his heart's desires, O Nanak, and his hope is fulfilled. ॥2॥
1300.4: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In the Saadh Sangat is the treasure of the Lord's Name, the helper ever at one's side, of use to the soul. The one who bathes every day in the dust of the Sants' feet takes away the sins of birth after birth. Lofty is the word of the Sants; remembering it again and again, mortals have crossed over, O Nanak. ॥2॥
1300.5: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Through the Saadh, sing the praises of the Lord, Har Hare. Mind, body, wealth and breath of life are God's; remembering (him), sorrow departs. Why are you lured here and there? Attach (your) mind to the One. Most holy is the seat of the Sants; joining (their) company, meditate on Gobind. Leaving all else, Nanak has come to (your) refuge; unite (him with yourself). ॥3॥
1300.6: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Seeing again and again my own Friend, God, who stands apart (from all), I blossom with joy. (He) is the very form of bliss, peace and Sahaj; there is no other like him. A single remembrance of the Lord, Har Har, wipes out millions of sins. Dwelling on (his) virtues, sorrows are destroyed, and peace comes to the heart. Drink the essence of Amrit with (your) tongue, O Nanak, and be dyed in the Lord's love. ॥4॥
1301.1: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O friends, O Sants, come to my home. Singing (God's) praises there is bliss and joy, (and) sins are erased and driven far off. I place the Sants' feet on my forehead, and light comes into the dark house. By the Sants' grace the lotus (of the heart) blossoms; seeing Gobind near, I dwell on him. By the grace of God (I) have found the Sants; Nanak is a sacrifice, a sacrifice to that moment. ॥4॥
1301.2: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Gopal, (I have come to) the refuge of your feet. From attachment, pride, deceit and doubt save (me), cutting away (their) fetters. Those drowning in the world-ocean have been saved by remembering the Lord, the mine of jewels. O Lord, your Name is cooling; my Master, God, is perfect. Removing the pain of the lowly, (he) carries (them) across; the Lord is the treasure of mercy, the saviour of the fallen. Through the pains of millions of births (this human life) has been gained; Nanak is at peace: the Guru has made the Naam firm (within him). ॥4॥
1301.3: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Blessed is that love which is fixed on (God's) feet; (through it) the joys of millions of recitations and austerities are gained; by great good fortune the Perfect One has come and met (me). I, helpless, am your slave, your servant; every other shelter I have given up. Remembering God, even the specks of doubt are cut away; receiving the salve of wisdom, I who slept have woken. You are unfathomable, utterly great, O Master, an ocean of mercy, perfect, a mine of jewels. Nanak, a beggar, pleads for the Lord's Name, Har Har; (he) has come and laid his forehead at God's feet. ॥2॥
1301.4: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (We are) unclean, hard-hearted, deceitful and lustful; as you know best, carry (us) across, O Master. You are all-powerful, able to give refuge; you protect, exercising your own power. Recitation, austerity, vows, ritual purity and self-restraint: by these ways there is no release. O God, casting (your) glance of grace, draw Nanak out of the deep, dark pit. ॥2॥
1301.5: Raag Kanra, Ghar 4, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (The Guru) who bows to Narayan, the King of men: to such a Guru one should be a sacrifice, again and again; himself free, he carries me across. Which, which, which of (his) virtues should one tell? There is no end and no far shore to them. Among lakhs, lakhs, lakhs and many crores, there is hardly one who reflects in this way. I am struck with wonder, wonder, nothing but wonder, at the deep crimson dye of the Beloved. Says Nanak, the Sants taste its relish, as a mute tastes (a sweet) and only smiles. ॥2॥
1302.1: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Sants have known none other than God; seeing (him) alike in all, high and low, (they) speak (of him) with the mouth and hold (him) in the mind. In every heart he is present, the ocean of peace, the destroyer of fear, my breath of life. Light has come to the mind and doubt is dispelled, (since) the Guru gave the mantra into (my) ear. (The Sants) keep reflecting on (God), who knows all that is done, full of compassion, the knower of hearts. At all hours Nanak sings (his) praise, to beg for the gift of the Lord. ॥2॥
1302.2: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Many, so many are those who talk and get talked about; (but) rare is such a servant who knows union with the Essence (of all). (For him) there is no sorrow, all is joy, O brother; with (his) eyes (he sees) the One alone. Nothing is bad, all is good, O brother; there is no defeat, all is victory. There is no grief, (he) is ever joyful, O brother; leaving (this joy), he takes up nothing (else). Says Nanak, (such) a servant is (one with) the Lord, Har Har Har; where does he come, where does he go? ॥2॥
1302.3: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). May the Beloved of (my) heart never be forgotten. (My) body and mind are absorbed in him; (yet) the enchantress (Maya) is enchanting (me), O my mother. Whoever I tell my pain to, they too, they too are held fast and stuck. It is one net of many kinds; its knot cannot be loosed. Wandering and wandering, servant Nanak has come to the refuge of the Sants alone; ignorance, doubt and attachment to Maya are cut away, and (God) has taken (him) into his embrace. ॥2॥
1302.4: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In my (heart) there are bliss, delight and joy: singing the Name, meditating on the Name; the Name is the support of our life. The Name is (our) wisdom, the Name (our) cleansing bath; the Lord's Name sets our affairs right. The Lord's Name is (our) glory, the Name (our) greatness; the Lord's Name carries (us) across the treacherous, terrifying world-ocean. The inaccessible treasure, the priceless ruby, has been obtained at the Guru's feet. Says Nanak, God has shown mercy, and (we) are rapt in heart at the sight of him. ॥2॥
1302.5: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Friend, the companion, the Master (God) is near. At the side of all, (he) sees and hears; why do (you) do wrong for so small a gain? Apart from the Naam, all that (you) cling to is nothing; nothing of it is yours. Hereafter all comes plainly into view; here (you) are beguiled in the darkness of doubt. (You) are held fast by son, wife and Maya, and have forgotten the Giver who bestows (all). Says Nanak, (my) trust is in the One alone; my Guru is the cutter of bonds. ॥2॥
1303.1: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O God,) your Sants have trampled down the army of vice. O Master, (I lean on) your support and trust in you; (I) have longed for your refuge. Meeting (your) sight, (I) have wiped out the great sins of birth after birth. Light has dawned (within), a radiance of bliss; (I) am absorbed in the samadhi of Sahaj. Who says that nothing (can come) from you? You are all-powerful, unfathomable. O treasure of mercy, Nanak has taken (your) Name and earned its profit; (for him it is) love, beauty and delight. ॥2॥
1303.2: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The drowning mortal, repeating (the Name of) the Lord, takes heart; (his) attachment, doubt, sorrow and pain are destroyed. Day and night I remember the Guru's feet; whichever way I turn my eyes, (I see) your refuge, (O God). By the Sants' grace (I) have sung the praises of the Lord; on meeting the Guru, Nanak has gained peace. ॥2॥
1303.3: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Remembering the Naam, one finds peace in the mind; joining the holy ones, one should sing the Lord's praise. O God, show mercy and dwell in (my) heart; (may) my forehead (rest) at the feet of the Sants. O mind, remember the Supreme Lord. O Nanak, through the Guru, listen to the praise of the Lord. ॥2॥
1303.4: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In my mind is the love of touching God's feet. (My) tongue is sated with the food of the Lord, Har Har, and (my) eyes are content with the sight of God. The Beloved's praise fills (my) ears, taking away all sins, faults and filth. (My) feet run on the peaceful path to the Master, and the limbs of (my) body delight in the company of the Sants. (I) have taken the refuge of the perfect, imperishable (God); worn out with other means, (I) try them no more. O Nanak, (God) has taken his servants by the hand; (they) do not die in the pitch-dark ocean. ॥2॥
1303.5: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Deceit cries out and the ruinous wicked (passions) roar; death crushes (such people) time after time. Drunk with ego, steeped in other (pleasures), fond of false friends and taking them for beloveds, (they) wander through lakhs of lanes. (Their) dealings are with what passes, (their) conduct is without rule; drunk with the wine of mine-ness, (they) burn in anger. O compassionate, merciful Gopal, kin of the lowly, Nanak has fallen at (your) refuge: save (him). ॥2॥
1303.6: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (God) is the giver of soul, breath of life and honour; forgetting the Lord, there is nothing but loss. Leaving Gobind, (you) cling to others; (you) spill the Amrit and throw it on the ground. Clinging to the taste of vice, you fool, how can (you) enjoy peace? (You) are gripped by lust, anger and greed, the very mine of births. O purifier of the fallen, (I) have come to (your) refuge; knowing Nanak (as your own), save (him). ॥2॥
1304.1: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I behold the lotus face of Ram; searching and searching, (I) have found the jewel (of the Name), and all anxiety is forgotten. Enshrining (his) lotus feet in (my) heart, the wretched pain has lifted. For me Gobind is kingdom, wealth, family and everything. In the Saadh Sangat Nanak has gained (this) profit, and dies no more. ॥2॥
1304.2: Raag Kanra, Ghar 5, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Worship God, dwelling on the Naam; clinging to the feet of the Guru, the True Guru, you will find the unfathomable Lord in (your) mind; O brother, by the Guru's grace you will conquer the world. I have searched out many kinds of worship in many ways; that alone is worship which pleases the Lord. This (body) is a puppet put together from clay; what deeds can it do? O God, the one whom you take by the arm and set on the path, that being meets you. I can see no other shelter; mine is the shelter of the one Lord, and (in him) my hope. What prayer can a lowly one make, when God dwells in every heart? In (my) mind is a thirst for God's feet. Servant Nanak is called your servant; I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, ever a sacrifice (to you). ॥2॥
1304.3: Raag Kanra, Ghar 6, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O Beloved, your Name is the deliverer of the world; the treasure of the Lord's Name is the nine treasures. Many, many are the colours of the incomparable Lord; why, O mind, are you lost in attachment? With (your) eyes behold the sight of the Saadh; (but) he alone gains (it) on whose brow (this) is written. I serve the feet of the holy, of the Sants; I long for (their) dust, which makes pure; (it is) the bath at the sixty-eight (places of pilgrimage), which cuts away filth. Meditate (on him) with every breath; (he) does not turn his face away. Nothing of lakhs and crores goes along (with you); at the last, dear God's Name (alone) comes to (your) aid. In (your) mind's thought, hold to the One Formless Lord; give up all love of another. Which of your virtues can I tell, O Beloved? Not even one (of your) kindnesses can I describe. Great is the thirst in my mind for (your) sight; O divine Guru of the world, meet Nanak. ॥2॥
The nine treasures (nidhis): by tradition, the nine treasures of Kuber, the god of wealth; that is, all the riches of the world.
The sixty-eight places of pilgrimage are the tiraths held most holy in India.
1305.1: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). What is that way by which (God's) sight and the touch (of his feet may be gained)? (I) hope and thirst for (him) whose very being bears fruit; with longing (my) heart yearns. Humble, with a thirst like the fish's, let one be absorbed in the Sants, the Sants of the Lord; for the dust (of the feet) of the Lord's Sants, let the heart be offered up; (then) God has become merciful. When pride and attachment were given up, then, O Nanak, the dear Lord was met. ॥2॥
1305.2: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (God dwells) in hue upon hue, in all the hues of every hue; from worm to elephant, he fills all, at the side of each. Fasts, vows, pilgrimages with the Ganga too, (standing in) water and snow, going hungry and naked, performing rites of worship seated with the limbs set in posture, the rite of marking the six limbs with circles and tilaks: (all are in vain) without meeting the sight of the Sat Sangat. Restraining (the senses) by force to the extreme, (one) stays upside down, (hanging) head first; (yet) the sickness of Haumai takes hold, and the gap (from God) does not close; in lust, anger and fierce craving (his) limbs burn. He alone is free, O Nanak, who has (found) the good True Guru. ॥2॥
1305.3: Raag Kanra, Ghar 7, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Meeting the holy ones, (my) thirst is quenched, quenched entirely. The five thieves have fled, easily and gently, as I sang, sang, sang the Lord's praises in love of (his) sight. O God, such (kindness) as you have shown to me, to me, how could I show the like (to you)? Giving my heart, I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice to you. Having first fallen at the Sants' feet, meditating and meditating (on you), (I) have bound (my) love (to you). O God, what is that place of yours like, where (you) take thought for (your) creatures? Countless servants sing your praise. That one alone has met (you) who is pleasing (to you); says servant Nanak, O Master, (you) pervade (all); you alone, you alone, you alone (are there). ॥2॥
The five thieves: lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride.
1305.4: Raag Kanra, Ghar 8, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. One should give up conceit and pride; the dear, merciful (God) is watching; O mind, become the dust of the feet (of the Sants). (Take) the mantra of the Lord's Sants, (and dwell in) the knowledge of Gopal and meditation on him. Sing of Gobind in (your) heart, and set (your) love on the lotus feet of the enchanting Lord, merciful to the lowly. O merciful One, show kindness and grace; Nanak begs (of you) the gift of the Naam, leaving behind attachment, doubt and all pride. ॥2॥
1305.5: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The telling of God's praise, which burns away filth, is gained by meeting the Guru; there is no other means. Bathing at holy banks, the six duties, matted hair, fire-offerings, carrying the staff: (I have) no purpose in these. Efforts of many kinds, austerities, wanderings, many discourses spoken: none has found (his) depth or (his) place. Having searched through all searchings, O Nanak, peace (lies in this): dwell on the Name. ॥2॥
1306.1: Raag Kanra, Ghar 9, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (God is) the purifier of the fallen, the lover of devotion, the remover of fear, the ship that carries across. Beholding (his) sight, the eyes are sated; hearing (his) praise, the ears are content. O Lord of life, Giver to the helpless, O Gobind, (I,) the lowly, (have come to your) refuge. O fulfiller of hopes, destroyer of sorrows, Nanak has taken the shelter of the Lord's feet. ॥2॥
1306.2: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O merciful Master, (I have come to) the refuge of (your) feet; there is no other place. To purify the fallen is (your) nature of old, O Master; meditating on the Lord, (souls) are delivered. The world is a bog and an ocean of vice; blinded by attachment and pride, (souls) have fallen (into it), distraught with the entanglements of Maya. O God, take (them) by the hand and draw (them) out yourself; save (them), O sovereign Gobind. O Master of the masterless, protector of the Sants, destroyer of millions of sins, in (my) mind is a thirst for (your) sight. O perfect God, treasure of virtues, O merciful, kind Gopal, Nanak sings the Lord's praises with his tongue. ॥2॥
1306.3: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I would give away, I would sacrifice countless (other joys), for the joy of one moment of a night of union with my Beloved. Mansions of gold, beds of silk: O friend, I have no concern with these. Pearls, rubies and countless pleasures, O Nanak, are ruin without the Name. Plain dry food and sleeping on the ground (are good), O friend, (if) life passes in peace with the Beloved. ॥2॥
1306.4: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Break (your) ego and turn (your) face (to the Saadh Sangat); calling Guru, Guru, search (your) mind; turn (the mind) to the love of the dear Beloved. The bed in the home (grows) lovely and ease (comes) to the courtyard: break, O friend, break, break off (your) company with the five enemies. (The mind) neither comes nor goes; it dwells in its own seat; the inverted lotus has blossomed. The clamour of Haumai is stilled. O friend, Nanak has sung, has sung of God, the deep (ocean) of virtues. ॥2॥
The inverted lotus: the heart turned away from God, like a lotus hanging upside down and closed; turned towards him, it opens as the lotus does.
1306.5: Raag Kanra, Ghar 9, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Therefore, O mind, repeat (the Name of) the Lord, repeat it. The Sants and the Vedas say this: the path is hard; (the soul) is lost in attachment, in the fever of ego. Those dyed in and drunk with wretched Maya (suffer) the torment of attachment. Repeating the Naam, that one alone is saved whom (you, O God,) save yourself. By the glory of the Sants, O Nanak, attachment, fear and doubt are destroyed. ॥2॥
1307.1: Raag Kanra, Ghar 10, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Dear Sants, give (me) such a gift that my soul is offered up in sacrifice (for it). (My soul) is beguiled by pride and cheated by the five enemies, and, entangled, dwells near (them); I have looked to the refuge of the holy: rid (me) of the company of the enemies. (I) have wandered through millions of births and wombs; defeated, I have fallen at (your) door. Gobind's mercy came, and the support of the Naam was found. O Nanak, (this) birth, so hard to gain, has borne fruit; (God) has carried (me) across the world-ocean to the far shore. ॥2॥
1307.2: Raag Kanra, Ghar 11, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Of his own accord, with natural ease, (God) has come; I know nothing, and have shown nothing; God, (the giver of) peace, has met (me), an innocent child. Destiny has brought (me) into the Saadh Sangat; (the mind) goes nowhere, and stays at home; the treasure of virtues has shone forth in this body. (His) feet have won (me) over and made (me) give up all else; (he) pervades every place and all; with delight upon delight, Nanak speaks (his) praises. ॥2॥
1307.3: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Hard it is to meet Gobind, the Master. (His) form is beyond measure; (he is) inaccessible, beyond the reach of the senses, and pervades all. (He) is not found by talking or by roaming; nor is he found by many arguments and clever ways. Efforts upon efforts, many means, O brother: (he) was met only when (he) showed mercy. O God, kind, merciful, treasure of mercy: servant Nanak (is) the dust under the Sants' feet. ॥2॥
1307.4: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O mother, remembering Ram, Ram, Ram, (I see) none other than God; I dwell in thought on (his) lotus feet with every breath, night and morning. Setting (my) love (on him), (I) have made (him) my own; the bond does not break. The Lord, the treasure of virtues, is (my) breath of life, mind, wealth, my all and my peace. Here and there Ram fills all; (I) behold (him) in the cave of the heart. The Sants' refuge is the ship that carries across, O Nanak; (in it) the dreadful pain is destroyed. ॥2॥
1307.5: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The servant's love is with God. (O God,) you are (my) dear friend, my companion; in your house is everything. I ask (you) for honour, I ask for strength; give (me) wealth, riches and sons. (You are) liberation, the way of life and sustenance, the perfect supreme bliss, the supreme treasure. Through devotion in (your) fear and love (one) is fulfilled; Nanak is a sacrifice (to you) for ever and ever. ॥2॥
1308.1: Raag Kanra, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (People) go on and on with talk upon talk; yogis in meditation, men in holy garb and the learned roam and roam over the earth, the whole earth. (In them) there is ego, only ego; others (too) are fools, fools, fools, crazed. Wherever they go, go, go, death is (over them) always, always, always, always. Give up pride, pride, pride; death, death is ever near, near. Dwell on the Lord, Har Hare Hare; says Nanak, listen, you fool: without dwelling, dwelling, dwelling on (him), this priceless life is passing (in vain). ॥2॥
1308.2: Raag Kanra, Ghar 1, Ashtapadis, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O mind, repeat the Name of Ram: (whoever repeats it) will find peace. The more one repeats it, the more peace one finds; serving the True Guru, one will merge (in God). The devotees long (for the Name) every moment; repeating the Naam, (the devotee) will find peace. The taste of all other pleasures has left (him); without the Name nothing pleases (him). Through the Guru's teaching the Lord, Har Har, has come to taste sweet (to him); the Guru draws sweet words (from his mouth). Through the True Guru's Bani the Being, the highest of beings, (is found); (so he) fixes his mind on the Bani. Hearing the Gurbani my mind has melted; drenched (in the Name), the mind will come to its own home. There instruments of the Anhad sound play for ever, and the stream of a spring trickles down. (He) sings the one Name of Ram every instant; through the Guru's teaching the mind will merge in the Name. (He) hears the Name, the Name alone pleases (his) mind, and with the Name alone he is satisfied. (One may) wear many bracelets of gold, of gold, and have clothes made of many kinds, (but) without the Name all are insipid, utterly insipid; (he) is born and dies, and comes again. The veil of Maya is a heavy, heavy veil; it catches the home in a whirlpool and wears it away. Sins and vices are all heavy as slag; the poisonous (ocean) is hard to cross, and cannot be crossed (with them). The fear (of God) and detachment have become the ship; the Guru, the boatman, will carry (us) across through the Shabad. Through the Name of Ram one should meet the Lord; (so one) will merge in the Name of the Lord, Ram. (God) has set (souls) in ignorance and put them to sleep; setting them in the Guru's wisdom, (he) will wake them. O Nanak, by his own will, as it pleases (him), so (God) makes (all) walk. ॥8॥
Ashtapadi (ashta, eight; pad, stanza): a hymn of about eight stanzas.
Anhad (anahata, unstruck): sound that rings without being struck, unbroken; in Gurbani, the Shabad of God's praise that resounds within without a break.
1308.3: Raag Kanra, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O mind, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har: it will carry (you) across. Whoever repeats it attains liberation, and will merge (in God) like Dhru and Prahlad. O dear Lord, show mercy, mercy, mercy; (the Lord) in his mercy will attach (me) to the Name. In (your) mercy unite (me) with the True Guru; meeting the True Guru, (one) will meditate on the Naam. The filth of Haumai of birth after birth clings (to the soul); joining the Sangat, the filth will be washed away. As iron, clinging to wood, floated across, so, clinging to the Guru's Shabad, (one) will find the Lord. Join the company of the Sants, the Sat Sangat; joining the Sangat, (you) will taste the Lord's relish. Without the Sangat, the proud man performs (other) rites; he draws out the water and pours in mud. The Lord is the protector of his devotees; he makes the Lord's relish taste sweet to (his) servants. Every moment (he) gives (them) the glory of the Naam; through the True Guru's teaching (the servant) merges (in it). One should always stay bowed before the devotees; if people bow (so), (each) will gain the fruit of virtues. Those wicked ones who slander the devotees will waste away like Harnakhash. Brahma (is held to be) the son of a lotus, Vyas of a fish; (yet) by their austerities each is worshipped. Whoever is a devotee, worship him; (this) will end the delusion of all wanderings. Do not be misled by seeing high caste or low; Suk (Shukdev) fell at Janak's feet and meditated (on God). The leavings of the meal fell on (his) head, (yet) not for an instant did (he) let his mind waver a whit. Janak, seated on the throne of the Janaks, took the dust from the feet of the nine sages and put it (on his brow). O Master, show mercy, mercy to Nanak; (the Master) will make me the servant of (his) servants. ॥8॥

Dhru: the child prince who, slighted by his stepmother, gave himself to devotion and was given an unmoving place as the Pole Star. Prahlad was the son of the demon king Harnakhash (Hiranyakashipu) and held to devotion to God through all his father's torments; in the Puranas, God took the form of Narasimha, the Man-Lion, and killed Harnakhash.
Vyas is the sage held to have arranged the Vedas and composed the Puranas; his mother Satyavati (Machhodari) is held to have been born of a fish.

Suk (Shukdev), the son of the sage Vyas, recited the Bhagavat Purana to King Parikshit. Janak, king of Mithila and father of Sita, is remembered as a sage who stayed detached while he ruled. By tradition, when the Brahmin Suk came to Janak for teaching he was kept standing outside, and the leavings of the meal fell on his head, yet his mind did not waver. The nine munis: the nine Yogishvara sages of the Bhagavat Purana, from whom King Janak (Nimi) received teaching.
1309.1: Raag Kanra, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Through the Guru's teaching, the mind will sing (God's) praises with relish; if the one tongue became lakhs of crores, lakhs of crores, crores (of tongues), (the mind) would meditate (with them all). Sheshnag of the thousand hoods repeated (his Name), (yet) repeating the Lord's (Name) he can find no end (to him). (O God,) you are unfathomable, utterly inaccessible, inaccessible; through the understanding of the Guru's teaching (one) will steady the mind. (O God,) those who have repeated (your Name) are the good ones; on those who repeat the Lord's (Name), (the Lord) will bestow peace. Bidar, the son of a maidservant, was a mere lowly lad; Krishna clasped (him) to (his) breast and embraced (him). Wood is born of water; (so water) keeps afloat the wood that is its own. The Lord himself adorns the servants of Ram, and keeps to his own nature of old. We are stones, iron, iron and great stones; (God) will carry (us) across in the boat of the Guru's Sangat, as the weaver (Kabir) crossed over through the Sat Sangat; (God) is dear to the minds of the Sants. Standing, sitting, rising, on the road and on the way, (he) meditates (on God). The True Guru is the Word; the Word, the True Guru; (the Word) makes known the level road to liberation. While there is breath, with every breath (he) gains strength, and without breath too he meditates on the Naam. By the Guru's grace Haumai is quenched, and then, through the Guru's teaching, (one) will merge in the Name. The True Guru is the giver of life to all beings; the unfortunate one does not love (him). This moment does not come to hand again; (he) will burn in remorse and repent. If anyone seeks his own good, he will fall humbly, again and again, before the Guru. O Master, show kindness, kindness to Nanak; (the Master) will put on me the dust (of the feet) of the True Guru. ॥8॥
Sheshnag: the thousand-headed serpent of the Puranas, held to utter a new Name of God with every tongue.
Bidar (Vidura): born of a maidservant, a devotee of Krishna.
The weaver: Bhagat Kabir, of a caste counted low; his hymns are in the Guru Granth Sahib.
1310.1: Raag Kanra, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The mind dyed in the Lord's love will sing (his praises); (his) fears and dread have become the pure fear (of God); clinging to the Guru's teaching, (he) will bind himself (to God). One dyed in the Lord's love is ever detached; the Lord is near such ones, and will come to their home. If I receive the dust (of their feet), I live; (God) himself, in his mercy, will have it given (to me). Mortals are caught in double-mindedness and greed; on (their) raw minds the colour (of love) does not take. Then, through the Guru's word, (their) life is turned round; when the Guru, the Being, is met, he will dye (them) with (love's) colour. The ten senses, all ten, run about again and again; (the mind) in the three qualities does not hold (them) still for an instant. When one is won over by the True Guru, (the mind) comes under control, and he will attain release and liberation. The One, Oankar, pervades (all); all will merge in that One alone. He is one form, and the one of many colours; all he makes walk by his one word. Through the Guru (one) has recognised the One alone; becoming Gurmukh, (he) will make (him) known. Through the Guru one goes and meets (God) in his own mansion, and sounds the Anhad Shabad. (God) has created all beings and creatures, the whole world; through the Guru (one) will gain glory. Without meeting the Guru none attains (God's) mansion; coming and going, (he) will suffer pain. O my Beloved, (we) have been parted for many births; the Guru, in his mercy, will unite (us with you). Meeting the True Guru, great peace has been found; (the Guru) will make the soiled mind blossom. O Lord, Har Har, life of the world, show mercy; (the Guru) will instil in me faith in the Name. Says Nanak, the Guru, the Guru alone is the True Guru; the True Guru will unite me (with God) in (his) refuge. ॥8॥
The ten senses: of perception and of action. The three qualities (gunas) of Maya: rajas, sattva and tamas, under which all deeds are done.
1310.2: Raag Kanra, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O mind, (the Guru) will make (you) walk in the way of the Guru's teaching, as a maddened elephant is held under the goad; the Guru will make firm the goad of the Shabad. Restless, (the mind) runs and runs in all ten directions; the Guru holds it back, and fixes its attention on the Lord. The True Guru gives the Shabad within the heart, and lets the Amrit Name trickle into the mouth. Snakes are filled to the brim with venom; the Guru will put the Garur of the Shabad into the mouth. The serpent Maya does not come near him; brushing away the venom again and again, (the Guru) will attune (him to God). Greed, the dog, is strong in the city (of the body); in an instant the Guru will strike it down and have it driven out. (The Guru) has brought in and settled truth, contentment and righteousness; in the Lord's city (one) will sing the Lord's praises. In the mire of attachment the mortal sinks deeper; the Guru will pull out the sinking one and set him clear. Crying save us, save us, (his) servants have come to (the Guru's) refuge; the Guru will give his hand and pull (them) out. The whole world is a dream, all of it a play; (God himself) stages all the play. Take the profit of the Naam through the Guru's teaching and set out; (so one) will go robed in honour to the Lord's court. One who acts in Haumai and makes (others) act in Haumai will bring in the coals of sin and sow them. When death came, (those sins) brought pain; what he sowed, that (he) will be made to eat. O Sants, gather the wealth of the Name of Ram; whoever sets out with this provision will gain honour. They eat, spend and give away a great deal; giving the Lord's (wealth), no shortage comes. Within the heart lies the wealth of the Name of Ram; in the Guru's refuge (one) will find this wealth. O Nanak, (the one on whom God) has showered kindness upon kindness will shatter pain and poverty and merge (in the Name). ॥8॥
Garur: a remedy against snake venom, named after Garuda, the bird who is the enemy of snakes; it was ground on a stone and taken by mouth.
1311.1: Raag Kanra, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). (When) the mind meditates (on God) in the True Guru's refuge, (it changes as) iron becomes gold in the company of the paaras: the quality of the paaras comes into it. The True Guru is the great Being, the paaras; whoever clings (to his feet) will gain the fruit, as through the Guru's teaching Prahlad was carried across; the Guru will keep (his) servant's honour. The True Guru's word, (his) word, is sublime; through the Guru's words (one) will gain the Amrit. As Ambrik attained the immortal state, (so will one) who dwells on the words from the True Guru's mouth. (The one to whose) mind the True Guru's refuge, (his) refuge, is pleasing will dwell on (his word), holding it to be Amrit, Amrit. The True Guru has become kind to the meek; (he) will show the path, the way to the Lord. Those who fall into the True Guru's refuge are upheld (by God); God (himself) will come to protect them. If anyone aims an arrow at (God's) servant, (God) will turn it back and strike that very one with it. Those who serve the pool of the Lord, Har Har Har Har Har (the Sat Sangat), (God) will have honoured in his court. Those who meditate (on him) through the Guru's teaching, the Guru's teaching, the Guru's teaching, the Lord will embrace and unite in his union. To the Gurmukh (the Guru) is the Naad and the Veda; won over by the Guru, the Gurmukh will meditate on the Naam. (He) becomes the form of the Lord, Har Har, the very form of the Lord; the Lord will have (his) servant worshipped. The Saakats (those who have turned from God) have not made the True Guru (their own); those who turn their faces away the Lord will make wander. (They live) in the waves of greed, in the company of the dog; (the Lord) will set (them) on the carcass, the poison of Maya. The Name of Ram carries the whole world across; joining the Sangat, (one) will meditate on the Naam. Says Nanak, save (me), save (me), O my God; keeping (one) in the Sat Sangat, (God) will merge (him in himself).
Ambrik is a devotee king of the Puranas. Naad: the sound the yogis raise on their horn (singi).
Chhaka 1: one set of six; the figure marks the close of these six Ashtapadis of the Fourth Guru.
1312.1: Raag Kanra, Chhants, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Those who have meditated on Ram are saved; the efforts for Maya came to no use. Those who meditated on Ram gained all fruits; blessed, blessed are they, of great fortune. In the Sat Sangat they awoke, held to the Naam, and their attention was lovingly fixed on the One. Shedding pride, attachment and vice, (they have become) Saadhs; clinging to their feet, may I (too) cross over. Nanak prays: O Master, (I seek your) refuge; by great fortune the sight (of you) is gained. Meeting the Saadh, let us dwell on Narayan every day, and with relish upon relish sing the Master's praises. Singing (his) praises let us live, let us drink the Lord's Amrit, (that) birth and death may flee. In the Sat Sangat (the Lord) is found; one should meditate on the Lord, and pain does not strike again. Show mercy, O Giver, O Being, O Creator, (that we may) serve the Sants. Nanak prays: (those who) long for the dust (of the feet) of (your) servants are absorbed in Sahaj in the sight of the Lord. O all beings, dwell on Gopal; (in this lies) the full toil of chanting, austerity and self-restraint. Dwell ever on the Master, the inner knower, (and) the whole of life bears fruit. One should sing of Gobind and ever meditate on him; the coming (into the world) of that one alone is approved. (Remembering) the stainless Lord, Har Har, is chanting, austerity and self-restraint; the wealth of Gobind goes along (with one). Nanak prays: (O God,) in mercy give (me) the jewel of the Lord, (that) I may tie it in the hem of my robe. (Within her) are songs of joy, wonders and bliss, (for whom) in mercy (the Lord of) supreme bliss has come to meet. God, the Master, the giver of peace, has met (her), and the wish of (her) mind is fulfilled. The joyful music has sounded; she is absorbed in Sahaj, and has not wept in pain again. (He) has taken (her) and clasped (her) to (his) bosom, shown (her) every comfort; (her) vices and evil are destroyed. Nanak prays: (she) has met the Master, the Being of supreme bliss. ॥4॥
1312.2: Kanre ki Vaar: by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji); to be sung to the tune of the vaar of Musa. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Name of Ram is the treasure; through the Guru's teaching keep the Lord enshrined in your heart. Slay Haumai, the poison of Maya, and remain the servant of (his) servants. (The one who does so) has won the precious gift of human life; he never comes back defeated. Blessed, blessed are those of great fortune, O Nanak, who through the Guru's teaching have savoured the Lord's relish. ॥1॥

The pauris of Kanre ki Vaar and all its saloks are the Fourth Guru's. Musa: by tradition a warrior whose betrothed was married to a king; Musa marched on the king and brought them both back, but when she said she would stay with the husband she had married, he sent them both back with honour; the bards sang his vaar, and this vaar is to be sung to its tune (dhuni).
1312.3: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Govind, Govind, Govind: the Lord Govind is the treasure of virtues. One should meditate on Govind, Govind through the Guru's teaching; then honour is gained in the Lord's court. Repeating Govind, Govind, Govind, (one's) face is radiant, and (one is) foremost. O Nanak, the Guru is Govind, the Lord; meeting him, (one) has found the Lord's Name. ॥2॥
1313.1: You are yourself the Siddha and the seeker; you are yourself the yogi joined in yoga. You are yourself the one who savours every relish; you are yourself the one who enjoys every enjoyment. You yourself pervade (all); what you yourself do, that will come to pass. Blessed, blessed, blessed, blessed, blessed is the True Guru's Sat Sangat, joining which (one) utters the words of the Lord's praise. All of you, say with your mouths: Har Har Hare, Har Har Hare; uttering (the Name of) the Lord, all sins will be washed away. ॥1॥
1313.2: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). (This) is the Name of the Lord, Har Har Har Har; some rare one gains it through the Guru. (In him) Haumai and possessiveness are destroyed, and (he) washes out evil-mindedness. O Nanak, he utters (God's) praises night and day; (this falls to) those for whom it is written from the start. ॥1॥
1313.3: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Lord himself is the home of mercy; what the Lord himself does, that comes to be. The Lord himself pervades (all); there is no other as great as the Lord. What pleases the Lord God, that happens; what the Lord God does, that comes to be. No one has found (his) worth; that Lord God is boundless. O Nanak, when the Lord is praised through the Guru, body and mind become cool. ॥2॥
1313.4: Your light is in all, O life of the world; you, O Lord, are in every heart, the dyer who dyes (it with love). O my Beloved, all meditate on you; you are true, true, O Being, O Stainless One. (You), the One, are the Giver, and all the world is a beggar; all beg of the Lord, asking their asks. Servant and Master, all is you, you alone; through the Guru's teaching the Lord is (seen to be) the best of the good. All of you, say with your mouths: Rikhikes Hare, Rikhikes Hare, through whom (all) gain every fruit. ॥2॥
Rikhikes (Hrishikesha, the lord of the senses): a name of Vishnu; in Gurbani, a name of God.
1313.5: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Meditate, O mind, on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, (and you) will gain honour in the Lord's court. Whatever (you) wish, that fruit (God) will give; through the Guru's Shabad attention is fixed (on him). All misdeeds and sins are cut away, and the pride of Haumai comes to an end. Through the Guru the lotus (of the heart) blossoms, and the Supreme Self is recognised everywhere. O Lord, Har Har, O God, show mercy, (that) servant Nanak may repeat the Lord's Name. ॥1॥
1313.6: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is pure; repeating the Name, pain goes. Those for whom it was written beforehand, in their minds (the Name) has come to dwell. One who walks in the True Guru's will is rid of poverty and pain. By one's own will no one has found (God); O people, see (this) and satisfy your minds. Servant Nanak is the servant of the servants of those who have fallen at the True Guru's feet. ॥2॥
1313.7: You pervade every place and every space, O Creator; all the making is of your making. You have fashioned the whole creation in many colours, and brought it forth in many, many ways and kinds. In all is your light, and within that light you pervade; through the Guru's teaching you attach (beings) to yourself. Those to whom you are kind you unite with the True Guru; through the Guru's mouth you give the Gurmukhs understanding of the Lord. All of you, utter: Dwell on Ram, dwell on Sri Ram, through whom poverty, pain and hunger will all be taken away. ॥3॥
1314.1: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Lord, Har Har, is Amrit, the relish of the Name; enshrine the Lord, the Amrit, in your heart. Within the Sangat the Lord God pervades; understand (this) by reflecting on the Shabad. (Those who) have meditated in the mind on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, have killed the poison of Haumai and cast it out. Those who have not remembered the Name of the Lord, Har Har, have lost all their life in a gamble. (Those whom) the Guru, pleased, has made remember the Lord have enshrined the Lord's Name, the Lord, in the heart. O servant Nanak, their faces are radiant in that true court. ॥1॥
1314.2: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Lord's praise is the sublime Name; in Kalyug it is the most excellent deed. Through the understanding of the Guru's teaching (the gift of) praise is gained, and the Lord's Name, the Lord, (becomes) a garland on the heart. Those of great fortune who have meditated on the Lord, to them the Lord has entrusted his treasure. In the rites performed without the Name, (one) is ever ruined in Haumai. (As when) one bathes an elephant in water, scrubbing it, it throws dust on its head again. O Lord, in mercy unite (me) with the True Guru, (that) the One Creator may dwell in (my) mind. Those who, through the Guru, have heard and believed in the Lord, O servant Nanak, glory be to them. ॥2॥
Kalyug: in the reckoning of the Puranas, the fourth and darkest of the world's four ages, held to be the present one.
1314.3: The Name of Ram is the sublime merchandise; the Lord, the Being, is our chief. The Lord has made the play, the Lord himself pervades it; (he) has made the whole world a trader. In all is your light, (and you are) within the light, O Creator; all your expanse is true. All meditate on you; fruitful are those who sing (of you) through the Guru's teaching, O formless Lord. All of you, say with your mouths: Lord of the world, Lord of the world, life of the world, through whom (one) is carried across the terrifying world-ocean. ॥4॥
1314.4: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Our tongue is (but) one, O God, (and) the virtues of the Lord are beyond reach and fathomless. How can we, ignorant ones, repeat (them)? O Lord, you are great, beyond reach, unfathomable. O Lord God, give (us) sublime understanding, (that) we may fall at the Guru's feet, the True Guru's. Unite (us) with the Sat Sangat, O Lord God, (that) in (its) company we sinners may cross over. O Lord, forgive servant Nanak; O Lord, if you are pleased, (we) may be united in your union. O Lord, in mercy hear (our) prayer, (that) we sinners, (mere) worms, may cross over. ॥1॥
1314.5: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O Lord, life of the world, show mercy; unite (me) with the Guru, the True Guru, the home of mercy. Service of the Guru has become pleasing to us, O Lord; the Lord, the Lord has become kind (to us). All hopes and the stirrings of the mind are forgotten; from the mind the entanglement of household is gone. The Guru, pleased, has made the Naam firm (within); (he) has made us joyful through the Shabad. Servant Nanak has gained a wealth that never runs out: the Lord's Name, the Lord's wealth and riches. ॥2॥
1315.1: O Lord, you are great, great, great, great and high; above all, greater than the great. Those who meditate on the Lord, beyond the beyond, meditating on the Lord, Har Har Har, become (one with) the Lord. Those who sing and hear your praise, O Master, (you) have cut away their sins by the millions. O Lord, O Being, those of the understanding of the Guru's teaching, foremost, of great, great fortune, are known to be like you. All of you, meditate on (him who is) true in the beginning, true from the start of the ages, true before (our) eyes, true for ever and ever; servant Nanak is the servant of (his) servants. ॥5॥
1315.2: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Our Lord is the life of the world; (I) have repeated (the Name of) the Lord, the Lord, through the Guru's mantra. The Lord is beyond reach, beyond the senses, beyond reach; the Lord, Har Har, has come of his own accord and met (me). The Lord himself pervades every heart; the Lord himself is boundless. The Lord himself enjoys all relishes; the Lord himself is the husband of Kavla. The Lord himself puts alms (in the bowl) of the whole creation, all the beings and creatures he has made. O Lord, merciful God, give (us) the gift (that) the Lord's servants, the Sants, beg of the Lord. O God of servant Nanak, come and meet (us); we sing songs of the Lord's praises. ॥1॥
Kavla (Kamala): Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth; here Maya.
1315.3: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Lord God, the Lord's Name, is (my) friend; in my mind, in my body, in my whole frame is the Naam. Through the Guru all hopes are fulfilled; O servant Nanak, hearing (the Name of) the Lord, (the mind) is at rest. ॥2॥
1315.4: The Lord is sublime, and (his) Name gives life; the Lord, the Being, is stainless, and blended in all. Those who repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, day and night, at their feet Lakshmi serves always. The Lord ever cares for and keeps all beings and creatures; (he) dwells near (them), (yet) apart from all. He alone understands whom (the Lord) himself will make understand, with whom the True Guru, the Being, God, is pleased. All of you, sing the praises of Govind Hare, Govind Hare, Govind Hare; singing (his) praises, (one) merges in the Master of virtues. ॥6॥
1315.5: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). (Even) asleep, remember the Lord God in your mind; remain absorbed in the Lord in Sahaj, in samadhi. In servant Nanak's mind is the longing for the Lord, Har Har; O mother, the Guru, pleased, unites (one with him). ॥1॥
1315.6: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). With the one Lord alone is (my) love; the one Lord alone is in my consciousness. Servant Nanak's one support is the Lord God; from the One alone come salvation and honour. ॥2॥
1315.7: Through the understanding of the Guru's teaching the five sounds ring out (within); by great fortune the Anhad (sound) has rung out. (One) has seen Ram, the source of bliss, everywhere; through the Guru's Shabad Govind has thundered (within). From the beginning, from the start of the ages, the Lord has one form; through the understanding of the Guru's teaching (one) has dwelt on the Lord God. O Lord, merciful God, give (your) gift; O Lord God, keep the honour of (your) servants. All of you, call the Guru blessed, the True Guru, the Guru, the True Guru, by meeting whom the Lord has covered over (our) failings. ॥7॥
The instruments of the five sounds: the five kinds of instrument (strings, metal, wind, skin drums and pots), an image of full joy within.
1316.1: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The pool of devotion overflows; (its streams) run full to the brim. Those who have believed in the True Guru, O servant Nanak, find (it) by great fortune. ॥1॥
1316.2: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Countless are the Names of the Lord, Har Har; the virtues of the Lord, Har Har, cannot be told. The Lord, Har Har, is beyond reach, unfathomable; in what way can the Lord's servants meet (him), and unite (others with him)? Repeating the praise of the Lord, Har Har, and having it repeated, (his) servants cannot find (his) worth, not even a sesame seed's. O Lord, O God beyond reach, O Lord, attach servant Nanak to (your) hem and unite (him with you). ॥2॥
1316.3: The Lord is beyond reach, beyond the senses, beyond reach; how may I behold the sight of the Lord? If (he) were some object, he could be described; he has no form, no feature. The one whom (the Lord) himself gives understanding and makes understand, that person alone sees (him). The True Guru's Sat Sangat is the school in which the Lord's virtues are learnt. Blessed, blessed is that tongue, blessed the hands, blessed that teacher, the True Guru, meeting whom (one) writes the account of the Lord. ॥8॥
1316.4: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is Amrit; one should repeat (the Name of) the Lord in the True Guru's love. The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is pure; repeating and hearing (the Name of) the Lord, pain goes. They alone have dwelt on the Lord's Name on whose foreheads (this) was written from the very beginning. In the Lord's court those servants are robed (in honour) in whose minds the Lord has come to dwell. O servant Nanak, radiant are the faces of those who have heard (the Name of) the Lord with love in the mind. ॥1॥
1316.5: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is a treasure; it is gained through the Guru. Those on whose foreheads it was written from the start, the True Guru has come and met. (Their) body and mind have become cool, and peace has come to dwell in the mind. O Nanak, as (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, is uttered, poverty and pain all go. ॥2॥
1316.6: I am ever, ever a sacrifice to those who have seen my beloved True Guru. My True Guru has met those on whose foreheads it was written from the start. Through the Guru's teaching (they) have meditated on the Lord beyond reach; that God has no form, no feature. Those who have meditated on the Lord beyond reach through the Guru's word, those servants have blended with the Master and become one. All of you, say with your mouths: Nar Narhare, Nar Narhare, Nar Narhare; the Lord is the profit, and devotion to the Lord the choicest gain. ॥9॥
1316.7: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Dwell on the Name of Ram, who pervades (all); dwell on Ram, Ram alone, who is present everywhere. In every heart is Ram, the Supreme Soul; God has made the play in his own delight and in his own way. The Lord, the life of the world, dwells near; the Guru, the friend, has brought (this) to light. The Lord, the Master, the Lord God, has met those for whom love of the Lord was written from the start. Servant Nanak has meditated on the Naam; through the Guru's word (he) has repeated (it) in mind and consciousness. ॥1॥
1317.1: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Seek out and find the Lord God, the friend; by fortune, by great fortune, (he) comes to dwell (in the heart). O Nanak, the Perfect Guru has shown (him), and the mind is attuned to the Lord. ॥2॥
1317.2: Blessed, blessed is that lovely and fruitful moment in which the Lord's service became pleasing to the mind. Tell the Lord's story, O my Gursikhs, the story of my Lord God, who is beyond telling. How may one find, how may one see my Lord God, so finely made, so all-knowing? The Lord himself unites and shows (himself); through the Guru's words (the soul) merges in the Naam. Nanak is a sacrifice to those who repeat (the Name of) the Lord, who is free of all desire. ॥10॥
1317.3: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The eyes are dyed with (the love of) the Lord God (in those to whom) the Guru gives the collyrium of wisdom. I have found God, (my) friend; O servant Nanak, (he) has met (me) in Sahaj. ॥1॥
1317.4: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Within the Gurmukh is peace; in mind and body he is merged in the Name. He thinks of the Name, reads the Name alone, and stays attuned in love to the Name. The precious gift of the Name is gained, and his anxiety has vanished. On meeting the True Guru the Name wells up, and all thirst and hunger go. O Nanak, steeped in the Name, one gains the Name alone. ॥2॥
1317.5: You yourself created the world, and you yourself brought it under (your) sway. Some he has made manmukhs and caused to lose; some he has united with the Guru, and they have won. Sublime is the Lord, sublime the Name of the Lord God; a fortunate one has taken it through the Guru's word. All pain and poverty were taken away when the Guru gave the Name of the Lord. All of you, serve Mohan, the mind's enticer, the world's enticer, who brought the world into being and put it all under his sway. ॥11॥
1317.6: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Within the mind is the disease of Haumai; the manmukhs, the wicked, are lost in doubt. O Nanak, meet the True Guru, the Saadh, the friend, and be rid of this disease. ॥1॥
1317.7: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Mind and body are glorious then alone, when with (my) eyes I behold the Lord. O Nanak, (when) that God meets me, I live on hearing his call. ॥2॥
1317.8: O Lord of the world, Lord of the universe, Creator, beyond the beyond, (you are) the all-pervading Being, beyond weighing. Meditate on the Lord's Name, O my Gursikhs; sublime is the Lord, priceless the Lord's Name. Those who have meditated (on him) in the heart day and night have met the Lord; (of this there is) no doubt. By great fortune one finds the Sangat; perfect is the word of the Guru, the True Guru. All of you, meditate on Nar Narayan, Narayan, through whom the quarrel and wrangling of Jam have ended. ॥12॥
1317.9: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Fools aimed arrows at the Lord's servants as they uttered (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har. O Nanak, the Lord's servants were saved, attuned to the Lord; the one who aimed was struck himself, (the arrow) turning back. ॥1॥
1318.1: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). (Those whose) eyes have been drawn by love behold the Name of the Lord, Har Har. If they look upon another, O servant Nanak, they are cast out (from his door). ॥2॥
1318.2: In water, on land and in the sky, he alone is pervading, the One beyond the beyond. He cherishes all beings and creatures; what he does, that comes to pass. Mother, father, son, brother, friend: there is none but him. He is pervading within every heart; O people, let any of you meditate (on him). All of you, repeat the praises of Gopal, who is manifest in all the world. ॥13॥
1318.3: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Those who have met through the Guru are (true) friends; they have gained the love of the Lord God. O servant Nanak, praise the Naam, and go to the (Lord's) court in carefree joy. ॥1॥
1318.4: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O Lord, you alone are the Giver of all; all beings are yours. All worship you alone; you give (them) gifts, O Beloved. The Lord, the Giver, the Bountiful, put forth (his) hand, and rain fell on the world. Tilling the field of love, the grain has sprung up, and (one) keeps the Lord's Name (in the heart). Servant Nanak begs a gift (of you), O God: the support of the Lord's Name. ॥2॥
1318.5: The wish of the mind is fulfilled; one should repeat (the Name of) the ocean of peace. Through the Guru's Shabad one should worship the feet of the Lord, the mine of jewels. Joining the Saadh's company, one is delivered, and the paper (of the account) of Jam is torn up. Repeating (the Name of) the Lord, who is free of attachment, one wins the precious gift of human life. All of you, fall into the True Guru's refuge, (and) the stain of pain is wiped out. ॥14॥
1318.6: Salok, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). I go searching for my Friend, (yet) the Friend is with me. O servant Nanak, the Unseen cannot be seen; the Gurmukhs show (him). ॥1॥
1318.7: By the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). That True One has kindled love in Nanak; without him (Nanak) cannot live. When the True Guru is met, the Perfect One is found, and the tongue is steeped in the Lord's relish. ॥2॥
1318.8: Whoever sings, whoever hears, whoever utters and recites (the Lord's praise), the filth of birth upon birth is washed off (him), and he gains what the mind longs for. Coming and going is ended (for one who) sings the Lord's praises. (Such ones) themselves cross over and carry their companions across; he carries all (his) family across. Servant Nanak is a sacrifice to the one who is pleasing to my Lord God.
1318.9: Raag Kanra, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Such is the Sovereign Lord (Ram Rai), the inner knower, as a face is plainly seen in a mirror. He dwells in every heart; no smear clings to him, no stain. He is free of bonds; (in bonds) he is never seen. Look at the face (seen) in water, as it is: such is Nama's Master, Bithal. ॥2॥

1294.1: Raag Kanra, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).

There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
Meeting the holy ones, my mind has turned green (with life).
To the holy ones I offer myself, a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice, a sacrifice; joining (their) company, I have crossed over (the world-ocean).
O Lord, Har Har, O God, show your mercy; I have fallen at the feet of the holy ones.
Blessed, blessed are the holy ones who have known the Lord God; meeting the Saadh (the holy one), even the fallen one is saved.
The mind wanders and wanders in many, many ways; meeting the Saadh, (it) has been brought under control,
as the fisherman cast his net in the water, caught the fish and carried it off, held fast.
Good and noble are the Sants (saints) of the Lord, the Sants; meeting the Sants, the filth (of the mind) has been washed off.
All the sin of Haumai (ego) has gone out, as a cloth is made (clean) with soap.
The Master wrote (it) on (my) forehead, on my brow, from the very beginning; (so I) have set the feet of the Guru, the True Guru, in (my) heart.
